proposals.relationship: Burnette contrasts Pinchbeck’s assessment of women’s withdrawal from paid work with Davidoff and her coauthor’s emphasis on lost earning opportunities and marital dependence.
proposals.evidence_note: In the complete EH.net review, Burnette calls Pinchbeck’s overall benefits judgment controversial and juxtaposes her interpretation of withdrawal as leisure with Davidoff and Hall’s joint Family Fortunes (1987),273, on marriage becoming a survival route for middle-class women. This is Burnette’s named scholarly comparison of differing interpretations, with class scope and joint credit retained. It does not establish that the coauthors explicitly criticized Pinchbeck, directly adopted her method, or analyzed identical women. Pinchbeck’s own introduction4 acknowledges severe transitional loss, and7/10–11/22 show distinctions among farmers’ wives, dairywomen and cottagers. Original Family Fortunes passage and complete Pinchbeck conclusion remain unread.
primary_locators: Burnette EH.net review, paragraph beginning Pinchbeck’s most controversial conclusion and following paragraph quoting Davidoff and Hall
